Why go: a private boat and dinner facing the sunset

The Five Islands sit just off Taling Ngam on Samui's south-west coast, the side of the island that faces the sunset. A longtail boat is the traditional way to see them: low to the water, slow enough to look into the limestone cliffs, and private, so the timing is yours.

The evening finishes with a long Thai seafood dinner on the beach as the sun drops behind the islands. It is one of the most relaxed sunset options on Koh Samui and a good choice for anniversaries and proposals.

Thai or deluxe dinner

The Thai menu is already a full meal: two soups, a duck curry, seafood baked in coconut, sea bass with lemongrass, vegetables, rice and fruit, plus a cocktail. The deluxe menu adds batter-fried prawns, a 600 g lobster with cashews and crab with garlic and pepper, so choose it for a celebration or a seafood-loving group. The restaurant is an open-air Thai sala on Taling Ngam beach with tables inside and on the sand; ask for a beach table when you book if you want the sunset view.

Who it suits

  • Couples marking a special occasion.
  • Small families or groups of up to 6.
  • Guests staying on the west or south-west coast.

Who should choose something else

  • Groups larger than 6: look at a sunset cruise on a bigger boat.
  • Anyone who wants islands with beaches and pigs: see the private longtail to Pig Island.
  • Guests with mobility limits: boarding a longtail from the beach can mean wading.

Good to know

  • Longtails are loud and splashy: sit towards the middle and pack phones in a dry bag.
  • Allergies: tell us about shellfish or nut allergies when you book; the deluxe menu uses cashews.
  • Booking: online booking for tomorrow closes at midnight Thai time.
